newsitem.title: UGANDA: Uganda, Sudan talks postponed until January.
newsitem.headline: Uganda, Sudan talks postponed until January.

text.p: Iranian-mediated talks between Uganda and Sudan were postponed to January because Iran's foreign minister cannot travel to Uganda in December, an official said on Thursday.
Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni said on Tuesday talks between Sudan and Uganda would resume in Kampala this week.
But Minister of State for Regional Cooperation Rebecca Kadaga said on Thursday the talks needed Iranian Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati as mediator and he could not arrive until January.
The talks in January in Kampala would be attended by the foreign ministers of Uganda, Sudan, Malawi and Iran, she added.
Museveni said on Tuesday he did not expect any immediate progress at the talks as Sudan had not fulfilled its obligations under a previous agreement to end the dispute between Kampala and Khartoum.

Iran intervened in September and is supposed to verify accusations by both sides and sponsor agreements. Uganda and Sudan broke diplomatic relations in April. They accuse each other of backing rebel movements.

Under a pact signed in Tehran in November, Uganda and Sudan agreed to stop hostile propaganda campaigns, destroy rebel positions and supply centres, move all rebels and refugees at least 100 km (60 miles) inside their borders and encourage the voluntary repatriation of refugees.
Uganda accuses Sudan of supporting the Lord's Resistance Army (LRA) rebels in the north. Sudan accuses Uganda of backing the Sudan Peoples' Liberation Army, the largest rebel group in southern Sudan.
